text:
maria: heads up — apiserver 5xx spikes + controller-manager flapping in eu-west1 for the last ~4m. multiple GPU nodes stuck in Provisioning. anyone oncall? :eyes:
ajay: i can take this. any logs or events you can paste?
maria: kube events snippet:
```
Normal   Scheduled  2m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/gpu-job-42 to gpu-node-17
Warning  Failed     2m   kubelet            Error getting node info: Get \"https://10.0.2.5:6443/api/v1/nodes/gpu-node-17\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
Warning  Failed     2m   controller        failed to provision volume: rpc error: context deadline exceeded
```
oncall-bot: incident created (SRE-17645) — priority P1, impacted region eu-west1
lia: seeing a huge spike in etcd leader elections around the same time: logs show repeated \"etcdserver: leader changed to \" messages and request latency jumping >500ms. also control-plane host iowait is high.
todd: any recent changes? config, compactor cron, or snapshot jobs?
ajay: nothing deployed in last 2h. checked etcd metrics: compaction lag increased, and disk iops on /var/lib/etcd at ~92%. probable disk saturation causing leader elections.
maria: GPU provisioning backlog: 210 pending pods. scheduler log: \"failed to get node info: apiserver timeout\" — so scheduling blocked.
lia: quick mitigation idea: temporarily stop the nightly compaction job and reduce snapshot frequency, and throttle new GPU provisioning via admission webhook. I'll start with the compactor toggle.
ajay: doing a controlled restart of controller-manager on control-plane-2 to break any stuck watchers. commands i'll run: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/controller-manager --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=controller-manager -w
```
maria: please coordinate, don't restart all controller-managers at once. we have leader election there.
oncall-bot: scheduled maintenance window blocked — automatic rollback disabled for this thread.
ajay: restarted controller-manager on control-plane-2. watching etcd and apiserver error rate.
lia: compactor cron disabled (ran the toggle). also bumped etcd iodepth limits on the VM and raised the disk scheduler tunables for /dev/nvme0n1. will monitor iowait.
todd: thanks. also flagged a temporary autoscaler hold to prevent more GPU nodes from being requested. can someone add a note for product/customer-facing teams?
maria: added incident note with affected customers and mitigation steps. apiserver 5xx rate is falling — at 70% of previous peak. scheduler is now dequeuing provisioning jobs.
ajay: etcd request latency now down to ~120ms. leader election count returning to normal. controller-manager restarts didn't cause cascading failures.
lia: follow-up action items: move etcd to io-optimized volumes, add compactor rate limits, tune snapshot compression, and add monitoring alert for etcd iowait > 60%.
todd: long-term cost note: io-optimized disks + extra etcd replicas will add roughly ~15-20% infra cost for control plane per region. we'll include options in the post-incident doc for Product/SRE tradeoffs.
maria: assigning action owners: lia -> etcd disk plan + compactor tuning; ajay -> runbook update + safe restart guides; todd -> cost impact + approval ask. i'll own the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: runbook step completed: controller-manager restart verified.
maria: thanks team — observed GPU provisioning throughput recovering. closing active mitigation in 15m if stable.
lia: next steps in doc: add leader-affinity hints to reduce election churn and consider moving heavy control-plane jobs out of peak windows.
ajay: will also add a quick kubectl one-liner to drain problematic nodes that show long kubelet API timeouts.
todd: +1. will schedule a review with infra and product next week.
maria: closing note: no data loss, no customer compute lost, provisioning delay only. will update postmortem with timeline and metric graphs.
